title: Find Indices With Index and Value Difference I
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, an integer indexDifference, and an integer valueDifference, find two indices i and j such that the absolute difference between i and j is at least indexDifference, and the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at least valueDifference.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums of length n, an integer indexDifference, and an integer valueDifference, find two indices i and j such that the absolute difference between i and j is at least indexDifference, and the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at least valueDifference. Return the indices [i, j] if they exist, or [-1, -1] if no such indices are found. Multiple valid pairs are acceptable.
constraints: Find indices i and j whose absolute index difference is at least indexDifference.
Their values must differ by at least valueDifference in absolute value.
Return the first pair in row-major i,j order, or [-1,-1] when no pair exists.
hints: The constraints are independent inequalities on a pair of indices.
Enumerate candidate i and j in the documented return order.
Return immediately when both absolute differences meet their inclusive thresholds.
Exhaustive enumeration guarantees the first qualifying pair is returned and proves impossibility if none qualifies.
editorial: Exhaustive enumeration guarantees the first qualifying pair is returned and proves impossibility if none qualifies.

tests.explanation: Indices zero and three are far enough and their values differ by four.
The only sufficiently separated endpoints differ by only two.
